paragraphs.heading: Diagnostics
paragraphs.text: : S001 by the parser `internal/sketch/syntax` ([#195](https://github.com/cevr/ergo/issues/195)), and the other codes by the checker `internal/sketch/check` ([#196](https://github.com/cevr/ergo/issues/196)), which `ergo check` and `ergo diagnostics` run. The checker's code table (`internal/sketch/check/codes.go`) mirrors this page; a test keeps the table, the emitted codes and the rows below in step. `ergo build` and `ergo run` run the checker first, then lower the checked program from the checker's output (`internal/sketch/lower`, check-v1); a form the lowering does not lower yet is refused at build with S109 naming the ticket or stage that owns it, at its position, and nothing is written (`internal/sketchfront`). The checker's fixtures are in `internal/sketch/check/testdata/fixtures`; the prototype's fixtures (first line `// want CODE`) keep their outcome except the changes [the parity table](../../internal/sketch/check/testdata/parity.overrides) lists. The main compiler maps each rule to a code in its EF registry ([#79](https://github.com/cevr/ergo/issues/79); README Gap 18).

paragraphs.heading: Value-tied facts
paragraphs.text: : no compiler support yet. The parser refuses the clauses `given`, `gives` and `keeps`, and a `where` after a record type, with S001.

paragraphs.heading: Grammar
paragraphs.text: : the parser `internal/sketch/syntax` and the formatter `internal/sketch/format` implement the decided grammar of [#196](https://github.com/cevr/ergo/issues/196), and nothing else. The source is the appendix "Decided Go-shaped sketch" of the [2026-10-28 preview](../previews/2026-10-28-without-go-syntax.md) (62 productions), its decisions table and its seventh, eighth and ninth rounds. Where the sketch is silent, the rules below decide; each says why. A syntax error is S001 ([diagnostics](diagnostics.md)), with one exception, S108 for a type that mixes fields and operations ([Declarations](#declarations) rule 5).

paragraphs.heading: Public API inspection
paragraphs.text: . The text output is also the docs view until a separate doc generator exists. Inspection checks source; it does not run the program or lower it to Go.

paragraphs.heading: Go interop: `import go`, bindings and adapters
paragraphs.text: per section: **Binding files** and **Type mapping** are implemented by `ergo bind go` (`internal/gobind`, IG1), and the bindings of Go's standard library are embedded (`internal/sketch/std/gostd`). **Checking** is implemented (IG2): the checker reads the bindings, and a binding declaration in user source stays S109 (only a binding declares one). **Lowering** is implemented (IG3): Level 1 calls are direct Go calls. **Level 2 adapters** are implemented (IG4): a user extern names a binding's function and is checked against it. **Go modules** are implemented (IG7): go.mod and go.sum beside ergo.mod, stamped bindings under ergo.bind/. **Host calls** are implemented (IG10): a hidden `context.Context` that interruption cancels. **Go calls Ergo** is implemented (IG11): `ergo lib` exports a library's functions to Go, and an Ergo value converts to a Go interface.

paragraphs.heading: Resources and automatic release
paragraphs.text: : every rule below is checked, and the build releases what the rules release: resource types, the ownership flow of locals, parameters and temporaries, aggregates, containers and unions, tasks, structured lends and the providers a `with` builds. The [Visibility](#visibility) of releases in tools is designed.

paragraphs.heading: Runtime rules
paragraphs.text: : `runtime/rt` implements the task tree, stop propagation, masks, scopes, the context store and defect propagation. `runtime/v1` adapts them to lowered frames and holds the Go bodies of the std packages `task`, `scope`, `queue` and `timeout` ([Tasks](#tasks), [Exit actions](#exit-actions), [Queues](#queues), [Timeouts](#timeouts)); their Ergo signatures check ([stdlib.md](stdlib.md#v1-packages-task-scope-queue-and-slice)), and `ergo build` lowers their calls (check-v1 stage D3b). Each section's status says what is lowered.

paragraphs.heading: Standard library outline
paragraphs.text: per family: each package under `internal/sketch/std` is Ergo source that the checker checks like user code and `ergo build` lowers, with Go bodies in `runtime/v1` where a family needs the host; each family below states its own status, and a family with no package is designed. The prelude's `Console` (`Println`) and the `Sleep` of its live scheduler lower ([runtime.md](runtime.md#host-and-lowering-notes)). `ergo build` lowers `timeout.After` to its `runtime/v1` body, which takes its deadline from the program's `Scheduler` ([runtime.md](runtime.md#timeouts); `TestTimeoutAfterLowers`, `TestTimeoutDeadlineIsTheProgramScheduler`). The four v1 packages `task`, `scope`, `queue` and `slices` (named `slice` until std-align S2a) have Ergo signatures, which the checker checks like user code, bound to Go bodies in `runtime/v1` ([v1 packages](#v1-packages-task-scope-queue-and-slice)); `ergo build` lowers their calls (check-v1 stage D3b; `TestTaskGoAndTaskResults`, `TestErgoRunQueueOperations`, `TestErgoRunSliceWithCapacity`). The context packages `trace` and `log` lower too (#199 stage 4a; [Context values](#v1-packages-task-scope-queue-and-slice)).
